android.view.ViewGroup.content-desc: The morning sun streamed through the tall windows of M.R.W.N. University's main corridor, casting golden streaks across the polished marble floors. Students milled about in their usual chaotic rhythm—some rushing to early lectures, others lingering by lockers, their conversations creating a comfortable hum of noise that had become the backdrop of campus life., Kaelen Winterborne leaned against the wall outside Professor Hendricks' classroom, his spotted tail swaying lazily as he waited. His white snow leopard ears twitched at every passing sound, catching fragments of conversations, the click of heels, the rustle of backpacks., "Think she's actually going to show up today?" Ryder asked, leaning beside him., "Who?", "The transfer student everyone's been talking about. Evangeline something.", Kaelen shrugged, running a hand through his messy white hair. "Didn't really pay attention.", "Right," Blake snorted from his other side. "Because you never pay attention to pretty girls.", "I pay attention to interesting girls," Kaelen corrected with a cocky grin. "There's a difference.", Before anyone could respond, a shift rippled through the hallway. Conversations stuttered. Heads turned. The kind of collective attention that usually preceded something—or someone—extraordinary., And then Kaelen saw her., She walked through the corridor like she owned it, though not in an arrogant way. It was simply natural—the way she carried herself, the effortless grace in every step. Her long, wavy brown hair cascaded over her shoulders, and large, fluffy wolf-like ears with dark tips sat atop her head, blending seamlessly into her hair. Hazel eyes scanned the crowd with warm curiosity rather than judgment, and a dark gothic tattoo peeked from the collar of her fitted blouse, curling elegantly across her collarbone., She was beautiful. Undeniably, breathtakingly beautiful., But what struck Kaelen most wasn't her appearance—it was the way she seemed to light up the space around her. She smiled at a group of girls who whispered as she passed, and the smile was genuine, reaching her eyes. She nodded politely at a professor who greeted her, and the gesture felt sincere rather than performative., "Okay," Ryder breathed. "I stand corrected. That's the transfer student.", "No kidding," Blake murmured., Kaelen said nothing. His ice-blue eyes tracked her movement through the hall, watching as she navigated the crowd with an ease that suggested she'd been here for years rather than days., And then, impossibly, her gaze landed on him and—his best friend., She paused. Her expression shifted—from polite curiosity to something warmer, something that looked almost like recognition. As if she'd found what she'd been looking for., She raised her hand and waved—bright and enthusiastic, her whole face lighting up with genuine happiness. But her eyes were fixed on fok, not him. She practically beamed at the other girl, her tail wagging slightly behind her in an unmistakably friendly gesture., Kaelen blinked, glancing at fok beside him. "You know her?", Before fok could respond, Evangeline was already making her way toward them, weaving through the crowd with the kind of confidence that made people instinctively step aside., "Hi!" she exclaimed, stopping in front of fok with a radiant smile. "You must be fok! I've heard so much about you—all good things, I promise. I'm Evangeline. I just transferred here, and honestly, I was so nervous about not knowing anyone, but then I saw you and I just knew we had to be friends.", The words tumbled out with such genuine warmth that Kaelen found himself smiling despite himself. There was something infectious about her energy—something that made him want to be part of whatever world she inhabited., "Evangeline," he repeated, testing the name on his tongue. "The famous transfer student everyone's been talking about.", She turned to him then, her hazel eyes sparkling with mischief. "Famous already? That was fast. Should I be flattered or concerned?", "Depends," Kaelen said, his natural charm kicking in. "Do you like attention?", "Only when it's from interesting people." She tilted her head, studying him with an amused expression. "And you are...?", "Kaelen. Kaelen Winterborne." He offered a grin that had made countless girls swoon. "Best friend of this one here, and generally the most charming person you'll meet on this campus.", "That's a bold claim," Evangeline said, her tone playful. "What if I meet someone more charming?", "Impossible.", "Oh, I don't know about that." She glanced at fok with a wink. "I have a feeling your friend here might give you a run for your money.", Kaelen clutched his chest in mock offense. "Betrayed already? We just met.", Evangeline laughed—a bright, genuine sound that made several nearby students glance their way. "I like you," she declared. "You're funny. But I like her more." She looped her arm through fok's with an easy familiarity that seemed almost practiced. "Come on, show me around? I want to know where all the good spots are.", Kaelen watched them walk ahead, his tail curling with interest. There was something about Evangeline—something magnetic and warm and utterly captivating. She'd barely spoken to him, yet he already wanted to know more., Interesting, he thought. Very interesting., Professor Hendricks' classroom was already half-full when they arrived. The usual arrangement—tables for two, arranged in neat rows facing the whiteboard. Kaelen's spot was in the third row, near the window, where he and fok had sat together since the first day of the semester., It was their spot. Everyone knew it., Kaelen slid into his usual seat, dropping his bag on the floor with practiced ease. Evangeline had followed them inside, her presence immediately drawing curious stares from the other students. She didn't seem to notice—or if she did, she didn't care., "Hey," he called out, patting the empty chair beside him. "New girl. Over here.", Evangeline looked up, her wolf ears flicking toward him. "Are you talking to me?", "You see anyone else new here?" He leaned back, flashing his most charming smile. "Come sit. I don't bite.", "Somehow I find that hard to believe." But she was already moving toward him, her expression amused., She slid into the seat beside him, setting her bag down and pulling out a notebook. "Thanks. I was worried I'd have to sit alone.", "Can't have that." Kaelen propped his chin on his hand, watching her. "So, Evangeline. What brings you to M.R.W.N.? Besides my irresistible charm, obviously.", "Obviously," she echoed dryly. "And here I thought it was the excellent academic program.", "That too. But mostly me.", She laughed, shaking her head. "You're something else, you know that?", "I've been told.", Their banter continued—easy, natural, the kind of back-and-forth that felt like it had been rehearsed even though it hadn't. Evangeline gave as good as she got, her wit sharp and her humor warm. Kaelen found himself genuinely enjoying the conversation, more than he'd enjoyed talking to anyone in a long time., Then Evangeline glanced around the room, and her expression shifted., "Wait," she said, her brow furrowing. "Is this seat...", She looked at fok, who had followed them inside and was standing awkwardly by the row, clearly unsure where to sit. Evangeline's eyes widened with realization., "Oh no. Oh, I'm so sorry—" She started to rise, her ears flattening with embarrassment. "This is your seat, isn't it? You two always sit together. I didn't mean to—", "Sit down," Kaelen said, his hand reaching out and catching her wrist., Evangeline froze, looking down at where his fingers wrapped around her arm. "But—", "I said sit down." His voice was firm but not unkind. He turned his head to look at fok, standing there in the aisle, and something in his expression shifted—a flicker of consideration, quickly smoothed over. "Hey, you don't mind sitting somewhere else today, right? She's new. It'd be kind of awkward for her to sit next to a stranger.", The words hung in the air., Evangeline looked between them, her hazel eyes clouded with uncertainty. "I really don't mind moving—", "Seriously," Kaelen interrupted, waving a dismissive hand. "It's fine. You're new. You should sit with someone who can show you the ropes." He glanced at fok again, his smile easy and oblivious. "Besides, she's been hogging this seat forever anyway. Time for a change, right?", He didn't notice the way fok's expression flickered. Didn't notice the way her hands curled at her sides, or the way she swallowed hard before turning away., "Great!" Kaelen said, turning back to Evangeline with a satisfied grin. "Problem solved.", Kaelen raised his hand in a casual, dismissive wave toward fok., "Shoo shoo," his tone playful, almost affectionate.

android.view.ViewGroup.content-desc: Kaelen didn't even turn his head fully to face her, keeping his body angled toward Evangeline, though his tail gave a lazy, welcoming flick at the sound of fok's voice. He kept that cocky, half lidded grin plastered on his face, the kind that suggested he was having the time of his life., "My day was pretty average, honestly," Kaelen said, finally cutting a glance sideways at fok. His ice blue eyes sparkled with mischief. "But now that you're here to interrupt my excellent conversation with the new girl, I'd say it's gotten significantly more entertaining.", He let out a short, amused huff and nudged Evangeline with his elbow a casual gesture of camaraderie before turning his attention back to fok. "What about you? Did you manage to survive that nightmare of a lecture before this one, or did you fall asleep standing up again?", Evangeline was watching the interaction with keen interest, her hazel eyes darting between Kaelen's playful expression and fok's uncertain stance. "You two seem very close," she noted, her voice warm and genuinely curious. "Is he always this much of a handful?", Kaelen barked out a laugh, running a hand through his messy white hair. "Always. I'm a menace, clearly. But she's used to it by now." He reached out without thinking, his long fingers briefly brushing against fok's arm in a dismissive but familiar pat before he settled back into his seat.
